modules.name: Zairenkai System Module

magisk.evidence: Magisk docs/changes.md v21.2: 'Fix the magisk --install-module command'; the module's update-binary needs v20.4+

kernelsu.evidence: ksud cli.rs: module install|uninstall|list (tiann/KernelSU 6d31a61, KernelSU-Next b427a3f)

conflicts.reason: Another frame-aware scheduler writing the same cpufreq nodes (FAS docs/CAPABILITIES.md: running two FAS modules at once is not supported). Module id from shadow3aaa/fas-rs build.rs at 09ba876.
The earlier separate Core module; zairenkai replaces it and both would start zcored.
The earlier separate FAS module; zairenkai replaces it and both would start zfasd.

risks: zcored and zfasd start at boot from service.sh; each restarts at most 5 times in 10 minutes.

While running, zfasd raises cpufreq scaling_min_freq floors within [cpuinfo_min, scaling_max] and restores them when it stops (FAS docs/CAPABILITIES.md); service.sh runs zfasd restore after every exit.
Vendor performance agents may write the same cpufreq nodes; FAS backs off on contention but does not disable them.
Removing the module restores what zfasd changed, stops zcored (which restores any temporary override it made) and deletes /data/adb/zairenkai.

destinations.data: /data/adb/zairenkai/core and /data/adb/zairenkai/fas (customize.sh creates them 0700; config.toml in each is kept across installs)

lifecycle.startup: service.sh waits for sys.boot_completed, then supervises bin/zcored run --dir /data/adb/zairenkai/core and bin/zfasd run --dir /data/adb/zairenkai/fas, each with exponential backoff and at most 5 starts in 10 minutes, then writes <data>/failed; after every zfasd exit it runs zfasd restore
lifecycle.shutdown: the supervisors stop when the manager's disable or remove marker exists; zcored restores temporary overrides on SIGTERM; zfasd restores every floor it raised
lifecycle.uninstall: uninstall.sh stops zfasd and runs zfasd restore, stops zcored (waits up to 30 s), then deletes /data/adb/zairenkai; if the FAS restore fails it keeps /data/adb/zairenkai/fas and logs to /cache
lifecycle.recovery: disable or remove the module in the root manager (or its safe mode); <data>/failed and the daemon logs record start failures; zfasd restore restores recorded floors
lifecycle.kernel: Android 10+ arm64 (customize.sh checks ARCH and API); cpufreq policy directories for FAS (required_paths)
lifecycle.action: action.sh prints zcored ctl health and zfasd ctl status; KernelSU's WebUI serves webroot/ (FAS)
